messages.author: b17f4d0880547804
messages.subject: convergence issues with stan's optimizing()
parts:
Enter code here...
Hi all,
I'm trying to use stan's `optimizing()` function to extract point estimates from a large dataset.

The stan model I'm fitting is:
true_dbh_model <-'
   data {
     int<lower=1> n_obs;
     vector[n_obs] census_length;
     vector[n_obs] obs_dbh1;
     vector[n_obs] obs_dbh2;
   }
   
   parameters {
     real<lower=0> true_dbh1[n_obs];
     real<lower=0> dbh_increment[n_obs];
   }
   
   model {
     real true_dbh2[n_obs];
     
     for (i in 1:n_obs) {
       // Calculating true growth for fitted data
       true_dbh2[i] <- true_dbh1[i] + (dbh_increment[i] * census_length[i]);
       
       
     }
     
     // Observation error
     obs_dbh1 ~ normal(true_dbh1, 0.75);
     obs_dbh2 ~ normal(true_dbh2, 0.75);
     
     // Priors
     true_dbh1 ~ lognormal(1, 0.8);
     dbh_increment ~ normal(0,5);
     
   }
   
   generated quantities {
     real true_dbh2[n_obs];
     
     for (i in 1:n_obs) {
       // recalculating true growth for fitted data
       true_dbh2[i] <- true_dbh1[i] + (dbh_increment[i] * census_length[i]);
     }
   }'

 
  model <- stan_model(model_code = true_dbh_model)
 
 fit <- optimizing(model,
             data= stan_data, init = list(true_dbh1 = data$dbh_prev,
                                          true_rate = max(0,((data$dbh - data$dbh_prev)/data$census_interval))), hessian=TRUE)




Unfortunately I'm having trouble getting it to converge:

STAN OPTIMIZATION COMMAND (LBFGS)
init = user
save_iterations = 1
init_alpha = 0.001
tol_obj = 1e-12
tol_grad = 1e-08
tol_param = 1e-08
tol_rel_obj = 10000
tol_rel_grad = 1e+07
history_size = 5
seed = 1713917469
initial log joint probability = -2.33181e+07
Optimization terminated normally:
  Maximum number of iterations hit, may not be at an optima



However, I can get the model above to converge on a maximum if I run it in R's base `optim()` function using method "L-BFGS-B" where I supply the same initials and translate the model above as:

nll <- function(true_dbh1, true_rate, obs_dbh1, obs_dbh2, census_length) {
 #  P(true_dbh1 | mu_log_dbh1, sigma_log_dbh1)
  nll_true_dbh1 <- - dlnorm(true_dbh1,  1, 0.8, log=TRUE)
 
 # P(rate | sigma_rate)
 if(true_rate < 0) {
    return(-Inf) # Half normal - no probability of getting rate less than 0
 }
 
 nll_true_rate <- - dnorm(true_rate, 0, 5, log=TRUE)

  # P(obs_dbh1 | true_dbh1, 0.75),
 nll_obs_dbh1 <- - dnorm(obs_dbh1,  true_dbh1, 0.75, log=TRUE)
 
 # P(obs_dbh2 | true_dbh1, rate, census_length, sigma_obs_error).
 nll_obs_dbh2 <- - dnorm(obs_dbh2,  true_dbh1 + true_rate * census_length, 0.75, log=TRUE)
 sum(nll_true_dbh1,nll_true_rate,nll_obs_dbh1,nll_obs_dbh2)
}



Looking at the documentation of both `optimizing()` and `optim()` they appear to have the same tolerance of 1e-8.
I've had a look at the point estimates of each and they are pretty close though not identical.
Is there something I'm missing here, or are there any ideas/tricks to get this to converge?
Are there functions available to extract these point estimates? At the moment the output structure is a list with point estimates with one list as a named vector.

Cool, this is a new kind of question.  I’m interested in the answer, now that we’ve been thinking more about using Stan’s optimizer in various algorithms.  Just today I was talking with someone about using optimizing to get simulations for a model that could be fit using lme4.
A

Hi all,
I'm trying to use stan's `optimizing()` function to extract point estimates from a large dataset.

The stan model I'm fitting is:

```true_dbh_model <-'
    data {
      int<lower=1> n_obs;
      vector[n_obs] census_length;
      vector[n_obs] obs_dbh1;
      vector[n_obs] obs_dbh2;
    }
    
    parameters {
      real<lower=0> true_dbh1[n_obs];
      real<lower=0> dbh_increment[n_obs];
    }
    
    model {
      real true_dbh2[n_obs];
      
      for (i in 1:n_obs) {
        // Calculating true growth for fitted data
        true_dbh2[i] <- true_dbh1[i] + (dbh_increment[i] * census_length[i]);
        
        
      }
      
      // Observation error
      obs_dbh1 ~ normal(true_dbh1, 0.75);
      obs_dbh2 ~ normal(true_dbh2, 0.75);
      
      // Priors
      true_dbh1 ~ lognormal(1, 0.8);
      dbh_increment ~ normal(0,5);
      
    }
    
    generated quantities {
      real true_dbh2[n_obs];
      
      for (i in 1:n_obs) {
        // recalculating true growth for fitted data
        true_dbh2[i] <- true_dbh1[i] + (dbh_increment[i] * census_length[i]);
      }
    }'

  
  model <- stan_model(model_code = true_dbh_model)
  
  fit <- optimizing(model,
              data= stan_data, init = list(true_dbh1 = data$dbh_prev,
                                           true_rate = max(0,((data$dbh - data$dbh_prev)/data$census_interval))), hessian=TRUE)

```

Unfortunately I'm having trouble getting it to converge:

```STAN OPTIMIZATION COMMAND (LBFGS)
init = user
save_iterations = 1
init_alpha = 0.001
tol_obj = 1e-12
tol_grad = 1e-08
tol_param = 1e-08
tol_rel_obj = 10000
tol_rel_grad = 1e+07
history_size = 5
seed = 1713917469
initial log joint probability = -2.33181e+07
Optimization terminated normally: 
  Maximum number of iterations hit, may not be at an optima
```

However, I can get the model above to converge on a maximum if I run it in R's base `optim()` function using method "L-BFGS-B" where I supply the same initials and translate the model above as:

```nll <- function(true_dbh1, true_rate, obs_dbh1, obs_dbh2, census_length) {
  #  P(true_dbh1 | mu_log_dbh1, sigma_log_dbh1) 
  nll_true_dbh1 <- - dlnorm(true_dbh1,  1, 0.8, log=TRUE)
  
  # P(rate | sigma_rate)
  if(true_rate < 0) { 
    return(-Inf) # Half normal - no probability of getting rate less than 0
  }
  
  nll_true_rate <- - dnorm(true_rate, 0, 5, log=TRUE)

  # P(obs_dbh1 | true_dbh1, 0.75),
  nll_obs_dbh1 <- - dnorm(obs_dbh1,  true_dbh1, 0.75, log=TRUE)
  
  # P(obs_dbh2 | true_dbh1, rate, census_length, sigma_obs_error).
  nll_obs_dbh2 <- - dnorm(obs_dbh2,  true_dbh1 + true_rate * census_length, 0.75, log=TRUE)
  sum(nll_true_dbh1,nll_true_rate,nll_obs_dbh1,nll_obs_dbh2)
}
```

Looking at the documentation of both `optimizing()` and `optim()` they appear to have the same tolerance of 1e-8.
I've had a look at the point estimates of each and they are pretty close though not identical.
Is there something I'm missing here, or are there any ideas/tricks to get this to converge?
Are there functions available to extract these point estimates? At the moment the output structure is a list with point estimates with one list as a named vector.

--

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] convergence issues with stan's optimizing()
parts:
I don't have a good feeling for how optimization can go wrong,
but optmizing() has three different tolerances:

parameter values
objective value
gradient value

And each has both a relative and absolute form.

You can also run for more iterations than the default.

When you say the point estimates are close, you mean the one you
get from Stan even if it doesn't converge and the one that R's
optimize() finds? You could compare those results.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] convergence issues with stan's optimizing()
parts:
> On Jan 13, 2016, at 8:50 PM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:
>
> When you say the point estimates are close, you mean the one you
> get from Stan even if it doesn't converge and the one that R's
> optimize() finds? You could compare those results.

You can also compute the objective function (as computed in your R function, and as computed in Stan) at these values to (a) check that the Stan and R functions are giving the same answer (modulo an additive normalizing constant, as Stan currently does not compute these) and (b) see how close these two different “solutions” are in the objective function.

> tol_rel_obj = 10000
> tol_rel_grad = 1e+07
> history_size = 5
> seed = 1713917469
> initial log joint probability = -2.33181e+07
> Optimization terminated normally:
>   Maximum number of iterations hit, may not be at an optima
> ```
>
> However, I can get the model above to converge on a maximum if I run it in R's base `optim()` function using method "L-BFGS-B" where I supply the same initials and translate the model above as:
>
> ```nll <- function(true_dbh1, true_rate, obs_dbh1, obs_dbh2, census_length) {
>   #  P(true_dbh1 | mu_log_dbh1, sigma_log_dbh1)
>   nll_true_dbh1 <- - dlnorm(true_dbh1,  1, 0.8, log=TRUE)
>  
>   # P(rate | sigma_rate)
>   if(true_rate < 0) {
>     return(-Inf) # Half normal - no probability of getting rate less than 0
>   }
>  
>   nll_true_rate <- - dnorm(true_rate, 0, 5, log=TRUE)
>
>   # P(obs_dbh1 | true_dbh1, 0.75),
>   nll_obs_dbh1 <- - dnorm(obs_dbh1,  true_dbh1, 0.75, log=TRUE)
>  
>   # P(obs_dbh2 | true_dbh1, rate, census_length, sigma_obs_error).
>   nll_obs_dbh2 <- - dnorm(obs_dbh2,  true_dbh1 + true_rate * census_length, 0.75, log=TRUE)
>   sum(nll_true_dbh1,nll_true_rate,nll_obs_dbh1,nll_obs_dbh2)
> }
> ```
>
> Looking at the documentation of both `optimizing()` and `optim()` they appear to have the same tolerance of 1e-8.
> I've had a look at the point estimates of each and they are pretty close though not identical.
> Is there something I'm missing here, or are there any ideas/tricks to get this to converge?
> Are there functions available to extract these point estimates? At the moment the output structure is a list with point estimates with one list as a named vector.
>

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] convergence issues with stan's optimizing()
parts:
Ok managed to get it to converge by upping the iterations to 50k.

Also I had to turn hessian off as it caused a segfault when it was trying to return the maximised object in R.
This is probably due to the size of the samples I'm trying to maximise (200k). But what seems to happen is it uses about 500 mb of RAM as it iterates over the objective function and then when it saves the RAM usage suddenly maxes out.

Anyway when I left hessian=FALSE I didn't run into this issue.


I also see a github issue (https://github.com/stan-dev/rstan/issues/41) is already open about changing the optimizing() output so that the stan extract function can be used. 
Thanks for all your help.
